reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Young adult progressive conductive loss, normal drum: otosclerosis
Carhart notch is bone dip at 2000 Hz in otosclerosis
Weber lateralises to affected ear in conductive loss
Stapedotomy piston is definitive mechanical correction
reference.pathophysiology: Spongy vascular bone replaces dense otic capsule and fixes the stapes footplate at the oval window, blocking piston motion into the cochlea while inner ear initially remains normal.
additionalDifferentials: Conductive versus sensorineural loss by forks and audiogram
Tympanosclerosis versus otosclerosis history (infection versus family)
additionalInvestigations: Pure tone audiometry with bone conduction
High resolution CT temporal bone in selected cases
